hook: $15.98 curtains make a flat wall look architectural

scenes.visual_prompt: Bare wall panel set mounted alone with no drapery, mattress in frame, looking plain
scenes.on_screen_text: The panel wall alone still looks flat
scenes.voiceover: A $59 panel wall on its own still reads like four rectangles stuck to drywall.

scenes.visual_prompt: Reference shot of a boutique hotel room with floor-to-ceiling drapery along the headboard wall, away from any actual window
scenes.on_screen_text: Hotels drape walls, not just windows
scenes.voiceover: Boutique hotel rooms run floor-to-ceiling drapery along the headboard wall even when the window is somewhere else.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands mounting a curtain rod above and visibly wider than the panel wall
scenes.on_screen_text: Rod wider than the panel wall
scenes.voiceover: Mount a rod a little wider than your panel set, and the drapery visually extends the whole feature.

scenes.visual_prompt: Product graphic of grey blackout curtain panels with overlay showing 4.7 stars, 61,995 ratings, $15.98
scenes.voiceover: These thermal-lined blackout panels are $15.98 for the pair — less than a third of the panel set's own price.

scenes.visual_prompt: Dimmed bedroom with a single lamp on, panel wall and pillow stack glowing as the focal point
scenes.on_screen_text: Dark room = panel wall becomes the focus
scenes.voiceover: Block the daylight and the panel wall and pillow stack become the thing your eye lands on.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final wide styled shot of the complete headboard wall with drapery flanking it
scenes.voiceover: Sixteen dollars, and the ceiling reads taller than it is.

caption: The detail that turns a $59 panel wall into something that reads 'designed' instead of 'patched' is drapery that has nothing to do with an actual window. Breakdown and exact curtain pick on the blog.
